deep.reconstruction: Context (cote 154, 1983-84): Grothendieck studies the 'space' X of systems of n pseudo-lines (arrangements of n pseudo-lines in the projective plane). He describes it by a graph Gamma whose vertices are combinatorial types ('p.v.') of arrangements. These types are graded by degeneracy: stable (generic, simple arrangements), semi-stable, and 'superantique' (most degenerate, e.g. several lines concurrent). The edges of Gamma are specialization/generalization arcs. On the previous page he built 2-dimensional cell complexes ('surfaces représentatives') X_0, X_1, X_1'. Their role is to carry the pseudo-lines and the local systems, or parallel transport, of the combinatorial polygons Pol(D). He noted two defects. First, these objects are defined only off certain vertices or faces, which are loci of effective ramification. Second, the surfaces cannot be identified with one another inside X. This page starts a third variant, X_3, meant to remedy these defects. Construction: (i) delete the superantique types D_i from the vertex set; (ii) 'blow up' each superantique vertex; (iii) add new edges to Gamma linking the 'blocks' of types lying above D_i with the blocks lying below it, passing through its semi-stable (stable) neighbours. These new edges are transition arcs. They replace the superantique specializations of construction 2°, but they are no longer specialization arcs, neither progressive nor ultimate. He insists the corresponding elementary operation has weight 2, not weight 1 like the other moves. In the resulting surface X_3, which is fixed by the dual graph of Gamma, all the new vertices have order 4, i.e. the new 2-cells are quadrilaterals. They correspond to the triples (?) or edges incident to D_i, i.e. to the edges of the barycentric subdivision of the cell decomposition of D_i. In the stable case there are 2(n-1) of them. He concludes that each D_i embeds in X_3: vertices of the barycentric subdivision of the cell decomposition of D_i correspond to vertices of X_3. In modern terms, this is a resolution of the singular vertices of a 2-complex modelling the stratified moduli of pseudo-line arrangements. Codimension-2 strata are replaced by squares of weight-2 moves, so that every vertex becomes 4-valent away from the triangle-type cells. The goal is a genuine surface or cell complex presenting the fundamental groupoid of the space of arrangements, with Pol(D) as a local system on it. It is close in spirit to flip graphs of simple pseudo-line arrangements and the 2-cells of higher Bruhat orders B(n,2).
errors: The count 2(n-1) for the number of new order-4 vertices 'in the stable case' cannot be checked from this page. The handwriting around it is heavily corrected, so the exact claim (what is being counted) is uncertain.
The construction is a sketch. It does not say how the inserted edges glue to form 2-cells in all cases, nor how the result removes the 'ramification' defect noted on the previous page.

ideas.what: Graph Gamma of combinatorial types of pseudo-line arrangements, with specialization arcs graded stable / semi-stable / superantique.
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of the space of pseudo-line arrangements; poset of oriented-matroid rank-3 types; flip graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956, flip connectivity); Goodman–Pollack (1980s); Manin–Schechtman (1986) and Ziegler (1993) for higher Bruhat orders; Björner–Las Vergnas–Sturmfels–White–Ziegler (Oriented Matroids)

ideas.what: Blowing up the most degenerate (superantique) vertices and replacing them with transition arcs of weight 2, giving a surface X_3 whose new vertices are all 4-valent.
ideas.modern_name: Resolution of codimension-2 strata in a 2-complex presenting a fundamental groupoid; commutation squares and weight grading of moves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogous to Esquisse-style 'Lego' presentations (modular dimension); flip complexes of higher Bruhat orders (Manin–Schechtman, Voevodsky–Kapranov)
ideas.where_published: The weight/modular-dimension heuristic is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not for pseudo-lines.

ideas.what: Embedding each degenerate type D_i (via the barycentric subdivision of its cell decomposition) into the representative surface X_3.
ideas.modern_name: Barycentric subdivision / link of a stratum embedded in a resolved complex

missed.claim: In 1983-84 Grothendieck builds explicit 2-complexes ('surfaces représentatives') presenting the space of pseudo-line arrangements. The moves are graded by weight, and degenerate configurations are resolved into 4-valent squares. This parallels the later theory of higher Bruhat orders B(n,2) and discriminantal arrangements (Manin–Schechtman 1986, Voevodsky–Kapranov 1991, Ziegler 1993), and of flip complexes of pseudo-line arrangements, which were developed independently. It also ties pseudo-line combinatorics to his contemporaneous Esquisse programme of presenting fundamental groupoids by generators and relations of weight 1 and 2.
missed.quote: L'opération correspondante doit être considérée comme étant de poids 2, et non 1 comme les autres.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a Grothendieck-style 'Lego' viewpoint, with a weight filtration on moves and local systems Pol(D), on the topology of the space of pseudo-line arrangements. It could be compared with known results on the homotopy type of flip complexes and of higher Bruhat posets.

missed.claim: The variant X_3 is only sketched. Whether it actually cures the defects (ramification loci, failure of the surfaces to be identifiable inside X) is left open.
missed.quote: C'est pour pallier ce (ou ces) défauts qu'il peut être utile d'introduire d'autres variantes.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete, checkable combinatorial question: does X_3 give a cell complex homotopy equivalent to the relevant arrangement space, carrying Pol(D) as a genuine local system?

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical, heavily corrected sketch of one variant of a cell-complex construction within a little-studied manuscript on pseudo-lines. The overall programme is interesting and absent from the literature, but this page itself contains no completed result beyond a local combinatorial recipe.
